{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=methods+for+autonomous+problem+discovery+in+open-ended+intelligent+agents&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"The rise of agentic AI in drug discovery from static tools to autonomous virtual scientists.\", \"abstract\": \"Driven by large language models, AI agents are transforming drug discovery, enabling AI to break free from task-specific tools and advance toward the vision of autonomous virtual scientists. This perspective reviews applications across the R&D lifecycle. To evaluate system maturity, we introduce a 6-level \\\"Spectrum of Agentic Autonomy.\\\" We advocate for novel evaluation paradigms centered on full-chain traceability and outline adoption barriers, positioning AI agents as pragmatic scientist-in-the-loop co-pilots.\", \"doi\": \"10.1038/s44386-026-00075-0\", \"pmid\": \"42864384\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13658227\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1038/s44386-026-00075-0\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Autonomous Chemistry and Materials Innovation Driven by Scientific Agents.\", \"abstract\": \"Large language model (LLM)-based agents are reshaping how self-driving laboratories (SDLs) may support autonomous chemical and materials research. Although SDLs have enabled major advances in mechanized experimentation and closed-loop optimization, their scientific utility remains limited when tasks require literature-grounded reasoning, adaptive coordination, and interpretation beyond predefined search spaces. In this perspective, we examine how LLM-based agents may help bridge this gap by translating scientific intent into machine-executable workflows. We propose a five-module frameworkComprehension, Design, Execution, Analysis, and Optimizationto organize the capabilities required for agent-enabled SDLs, and we discuss representative systems, including Coscientist, ChemCrow, LLM-RDF, and AI-Chemist, as milestones in this transition. We also emphasize that agent-enabled SDLs should not be conflated with autonomous scientific discovery. Safety in physical execution, hardware interoperability, reproducibility, and auditability remain central challenges. To support a more critical assessment, we introduce the HYDRA framework for benchmarking trustworthy agent-enabled workflows. Finally, we outline a human-AI-SDL collaborative model in which scientists remain responsible for scientific framing, interpretation, and oversight.\", \"doi\": \"10.1021/jacsau.6c00213\", \"pmid\": \"42212086\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13213502\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1021/jacsau.6c00213\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13213502\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13213502?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"AI for science: Progress, challenges, and perspectives.\", \"abstract\": \"By 2026, artificial intelligence (AI) has completed a qualitative transition from specialized analytical tools to a foundational engine for scientific inquiry, fundamentally altering the paradigms of knowledge generation. In this review, we systematically evaluate the progress of AI for Science (AI4Science), characterized by the shift from text-centric generation to reasoning-oriented intelligence and the deep embedding of foundation models into the entire research life cycle. We propose a unified, closed-loop research paradigm comprising six core modules: literature research, data analysis, hypothesis formulation, experimental execution, report generation, and autonomous evolution. Furthermore, we synthesize breakthroughs across a broad spectrum of frontier domains-including information science, mathematics, energy, physics, chemistry, materials science, medicine, life sciences, astronomy, geosciences, and social science-highlighting AI's capacity for overcoming dimensionality constraints and enabling complex inverse design. We then identify critical challenges that persist, such as the scarcity of standardized high-quality data, the interpretability gap, and the physical consistency of generative outputs. Finally, we offer forward-looking perspectives on constructing cross-disciplinary scientific foundation models and fostering a future of human-AI collaborative autonomous research.\", \"doi\": \"10.1016/j.xinn.2026.101530\", \"pmid\": \"43011738\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13751209\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xinn.2026.101530\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13751209\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13751209?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Machine psychology for language models.\", \"abstract\": \"Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a \\\"machine psychology\\\" for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.\", \"doi\": \"10.1126/sciadv.aec1912\", \"pmid\": \"42950038\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13718702\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aec1912\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13718702\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13718702?pdf=render\"}]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "634b31a27a4166984384c271cc28916dd694f7e76214029946a6aa70d8bce2e0", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "unassigned_problem", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1038/s44386-026-00075-0", "doi:10.1021/jacsau.6c00213", "doi:10.1016/j.xinn.2026.101530", "doi:10.1126/sciadv.aec1912", "pmc:PMC13658227", "pmc:PMC13213502", "pmc:PMC13751209", "pmc:PMC13718702"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1038/s44386-026-00075-0", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13658227?pdf=render", "https://doi.org/10.1021/jacsau.6c00213", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13213502", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13213502?pdf=render", "https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xinn.2026.101530", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13751209"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}

Furthermore, we synthesize breakthroughs across a broad spectrum of frontier domains-including information science, mathematics, energy, physics, chemistry, materials science, medicine, life sciences, astronomy, geosciences, and social science-highlighting AI's capacity for overcoming dimensionality constraints and enabling complex inverse design.
